newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche news quells rumours, price still firm.
newsitem.headline: Roche news quells rumours, price still firm.

text.p: News that Roche Holding AG is buying U.S. food and beverage firm Tastemaker has dampened the speculation supporting the company on the Swiss stock exchange, but Roche certificates were still firmer on Wednesday.
Swiss bourse trade had favoured Roche recently, partly on speculation it would sell its fragrances and flavours division.
The latest news that Roche is buying Tastemaker disappointed some market participants who had expected Roche to spin off the whole division, traders said.
Comments by a Roche spokesman reinforced ideas that no such spin-off is in the offing.

"It (the news Roche was buying Tastemaker) is 180 degrees away from what people had rumoured. People had always rumoured that we would sell that division. But we have confirmed that our goal is to strengthen this business," said a Roche spokesman.
Roche preference certificates traded 25 francs higher at 12,310 francs in late morning trade here.

Since the start of the year, Roche certificates have risen nearly 20 percent, double the gains in the Swiss Performance Index. Some of the gains were linked to rumours the company was poised for a major acquisition, if not a spinoff.
The latest news has not fundamentally changed some analysts' favourable outlook for Roche.
Michael Hoehn, analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland, said his bank was keeping the buy recommendation on Roche.
Genghis Lloyd-Harris, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London, believed Roche was still strongly committed to the flavours and fragrances business, which has a somewhat uncertain outlook.
"They seem to be clearly committed to that business," said Lloyd-Harris, saying it appeared Roche management believes the prospects for the business "are better than most people realise".
He also believed that Roche paid a "reasonable" price for Tastemaker. The price was not published.
Despite what may appear to be a negative move, given an uncertain outlook for flavours and fragrances, Roche's overall picture remains quite healthy.
"The core business of pharmaceuticals and vitamins is very strong," he said.
He added CSFB still regarded the certificates as a buy at current prices, and was targeting 14,000 francs.
